svg.title: Banking transaction example: RPO 15 minutes and RTO 2 hours
svg.desc: These values are teaching targets, not measured results or fixed regulatory requirements. RPO concerns the time window of data loss; RTO concerns time to restore service. Each requires separate backup, recovery and exercise validation. Segments show the actual 15:120 (1:8) time ratio, with labels arranged separately to avoid overlap on narrow screens. This teaching example starts the RTO clock at incident point 0. Actual start and end criteria must be defined by business needs and recovery plans; this does not imply that every NIST scenario starts the clock at the incident.

g.font-family: Arial, Noto Sans CJK TC, sans-serif
g.text: Banking transaction example: RPO 15 minutes and RTO 2 hours
RPO 15 min : RTO 120 min = 1:8
Recovery point | 15 minutes before the incident (−15 min)
RPO (Recovery Point Objective) = 15 minutes: the target point for
data recovery.
Incident | 0 min
Timeline reference point: start of the system disruption.
Recovery target | 2 hours after the incident (+120 min)
RTO (Recovery Time Objective) = 2 hours: the target to restore
required service capability. The interval from the incident to this
target is the system disruption and recovery period.
These values are teaching targets, not measured results or fixed
regulatory requirements. RPO concerns the time window of data loss;
RTO concerns time to restore service. Each requires separate backup,
recovery and exercise validation. Segments show the actual 15:120 (1:8
) time ratio, with labels arranged separately to avoid overlap on
narrow screens. This teaching example starts the RTO clock at incident
point 0. Actual start and end criteria must be defined by business
needs and recovery plans; this does not imply that every NIST scenario
starts the clock at the incident.
